REGIONAL REGULATION OF PEKALONGAN REGENCY

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR

VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

heading: REGENT OF PEKALONGAN,
REGIONAL HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES
translated_text:
REGIONAL HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES

OF PEKALONGAN REGENCY

AND

REGENT OF PEKALONGAN

DECIDES:

To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN.

heading: CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Pekalongan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Agency for Community Empowerment, Women and Family Planning hereinafter referred to as BPMPKB is the Agency for Community Empowerment, Women and Family Planning of Pekalongan Regency as the institution that formulates and implements regional policies that are specific in the field of community empowerment, women and family planning.

jdih.pekalongankab.go.id

4. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
5. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
7. Protection against Gender is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, regional government, or other parties who know or hear that violence against men or women will or has occurred either temporarily or based on court determination.
8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or use of human rights, the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
10. Violence against children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
11. Victims of gender-based violence are people who because of their gender experience physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from State policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and society.
12. Integrated Services are a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and jdih.pekalongankab.go.id legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
13. Companion is a person or institution and/or body that has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a single unit that organizes integrated services for women and children victims of violence.
15. Medical Services are facilities that provide services that are clinical in nature in the field of diagnostics, and/or inpatient care for victims.
16. Social rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial condition disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning both in the family and in society.
17. Legal Aid is the provision of legal assistance to victims seeking justice who are unable and face difficulties in the legal field outside or before the court without remuneration.
18. Repatriation is the act of returning victims to their region of origin or country of origin while prioritizing protection services and fulfillment of their needs.
19. Social Reintegration is the reunification of victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
21. Service Standard is a benchmark used as a guideline for service delivery and a reference for assessing service quality as an obligation and promise of the organizer to the community in the context of quality, appropriate, easy, affordable and measurable services.
22. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a straight line up or down to the third degree.
23. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.

jdih.pekalongankab.go.id

24. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Pekalongan Regency.

heading: CHAPTER II
Article 3
translated_text:
Article 3

The purpose of implementing protection for victims of gender-based violence is to provide services and protection to men and women victims of gender-based violence and child victims of violence that occurs within the household and/or outside the household.

heading: CHAPTER III
CHAPTER IV
Article 6
translated_text:
Article 6

Physical violence as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (1) letter a is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or cause death.

heading: Article 7
translated_text:
Article 7

Psychological Violence as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (1) letter b is caused by acts that result in jdih.pekalongankab.go.id fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to the victim.

heading: Article 8
Article 9
Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

Exploitation as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (2) letter e is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs jdih.pekalongankab.go.id or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/orc. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities or indecency.

heading: Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

Maltreatment as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (2) letter f is caused by:
a. any act or action whether intentional or unintentional committed by another person that makes an individual sick or disturbed in their feelings, or receives an unpleasant feeling that makes someone sad, disappointed, annoyed, angry and afraid.  b. any sexual violation committed or permitted to be committed against a young person by an adult or another person legally responsible for them, including touching a child with the intention of sexual gratification or forcing a child to touch an adult, sexual intercourse, showing sexual activities to a child, pornography or allowing a child to engage in sexual intercourse that is not appropriate to their development.

Article 13

In carrying out the obligation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, the Regional Government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT) institution

Integrated Service Center

heading: Article 14
translated_text:
Article 14

1. PPT as referred to in Article 13 is established by the Regional Government by involving Regional Work Units, institutions, agencies and community organizations that have competence in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children.
2. PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is a functional work unit that has the main duties and functions of providing protection to victims of gender-based violence and child victims of violence in the form of seeking prevention, recovery, and social reintegration, providing legal protection, conducting coordination and, seeking to increase community participation, as well as monitoring and reporting

heading: Article 15
Article 16
translated_text:
Article 16

The complaints service field as referred to in Article 15 paragraph (2) letter a has the following duties:
a. conducting interviews and observation of the victim's condition; 10 jdih.pekalongankab.go.idb. making recommendations for follow-up services;
c. conducting coordination and referrals to services and certain parties and related parties according to the victim's needs; and d. conducting administration of the complaints process.

heading: Article 17
Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

The legal aid service field as referred to in Article 15 paragraph (2) letter c has the following duties:
a. providing legal aid to victims of violence both litigation and non-litigation.
b. making reports on the progress of legal handling.

heading: Article 19
Article 20
Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

1. The procedures and mechanisms for establishing PPT are regulated by Regent Regulation.
2. PPT Service Standards are regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

EMPOWERMENT OF VICTIMS

Article 22

Empowerment of Gender and Child Victims of Violence is implemented in the form of:
a. Empowerment of gender-based violence victims includes job training, productive economic enterprises and joint business groups with capital assistance.
b. Empowerment of child victims of violence who are not in school is to ensure child victims of violence receive the right to continue their education, and/or receive job training with capital assistance.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 23

1. The Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children.
2. The implementation of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out daily by BPMPKB.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

FUNDING

Article 24

Funding for activities related to the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out by the Regional Government is sourced from the Regional Budget, Provincial Regional Budget and/or State Budget as well as other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

jdih.pekalongankab.go.id

heading: CHAPTER X
CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 26

In the event of changes to the Regional Apparatus Organization structure, the coordination duties for guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children as stated in Article 23 paragraph (2) shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus responsible for Women and Child Empowerment.

heading: CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 27

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation.

So that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Pekalongan Regency.

ELUCIDATION

OF

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2014

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

heading: I. GENERAL
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

In order to prevent and address gender-based violence and violence against children in Pekalongan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for gender and child victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation. So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of gender and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts at the regional level, so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for gender and child victims of violence in Pekalongan Regency.

Article 1

heading: Article 2
translated_text:
Article 2

Letter a What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter c What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes a harmonious, aligned and jdih.pekalongankab.go.id balanced relationship between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Letter d What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death that occurs during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions Letter f.

What is meant by "growth and development" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.

What is meant by "survival" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.

Letter g.

What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Letter h What is meant by "openness" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among integrated service providers.

Letter i What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, religious leaders, social workers, police.

Letter j What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence experienced.

Letter k What is meant by "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen the victim, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.

jdih.pekalongankab.go.id Letter l What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure the victim is in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of the victim.

Letter m What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the victim's right to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.
